points.description: States what extension headers are: optional/additional network-layer information that extends the fixed (main) IPv6 header.
points.partial_credit: Half if only vaguely stated (e.g. 'extra headers') without saying optional/extra information extending the fixed IPv6 header.

points.description: States where they are located: between the fixed/main IPv6 header and the payload (upper-layer/transport-layer header), if present.
points.partial_credit: Half if only says 'after the main header' or 'before the payload' without both ends.

points.description: Gives one valid main advantage: new options can be added without changing the (fixed) header, OR packets with extension headers are processed faster/simpler by intermediate routers since most options are ignored (except Hop-by-Hop) unlike IPv4 where all routers process options.
points.partial_credit: Half if advantage is vague (e.g. 'more flexible' or 'more efficient') without the reason.

rubric.notes: Full marks need all three parts: what extension headers are, their location between fixed header and payload, and one valid advantage (either one from the model answer). Part marks go to vague or half-stated parts. A missing or wrong part loses only that part's marks.
